accepted.question_text: Given a p-compact group X, does there exist a sequence of finite groups G_0 -> G_1 -> G_2 -> ... and homomorphisms between them such that the homotopy colimit of the classifying spaces B G_i is homotopy equivalent to B X after p-completion? Equivalently, is every p-compact group a telescope of finite groups in the sense that hocolim_i B G_i recovers B X up to p-completion?
accepted.context_brief: p-compact groups and telescopes of finite groups

evidence.quote: Question 1.1 Is every p-compact group a telescope of finite groups? In more precise words, given a p-compact group X, does there exist a sequence of finite groups and homomorphisms {G0 -> ... -> Gi -> ... } and a homotopy equivalence hocolimi BGi ' BX, up to p-completion?

accepted.question_text: Let {B X_m}_{m in N} be a direct system of classifying spaces of p-local finite groups with maps f_m: B X_m -> B X_{m+1}, and suppose the homotopy colimit hocolim_m B X_m is homotopy equivalent to B X for a p-compact group X. Must there exist some stage m and a map g-hat: B G_p-complete -> B X_m, where B G_p-complete is the p-completed classifying space of a finite group or of a p-local finite group, such that the induced map from B G_p-complete to B X factors the given map to B X up to homotopy through that stage?
accepted.context_brief: factorization through a stage of a p-local finite group system

evidence.quote: Question 1.2 Let {BXm}m∈N be a direct system of classifying spaces of p-local finite groups and continuous maps fm : BXm -> BXm+1 with hocolimm BXm ' BX, the classifying space of a p-compact group X. Is there a map ĝ : BG∧p -> BXm , for some m, making the diagram ... homotopy commutative, where BG∧p is the p-completed classifying space of a finite group (or p-local finite group)?

accepted.question_text: Fix a homological degree s and let Sq^0: Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2) -> Ext_A^{s,2t}(F_2, F_2) be the squaring operation induced by the Frobenius map on the dual Steenrod algebra. If Im((Sq^0)^i) denotes the image of the i-fold iterate on Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2), does there exist a number r = r(s) such that for every i >= r the map (Sq^0)^{i-r}: Im((Sq^0)^r) -> Im((Sq^0)^i) is an isomorphism? Equivalently, for fixed s, is every finite Sq^0-family in Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2) bounded in length by some r(s)?
accepted.context_brief: eventual periodicity of Sq^0 on Ext over the Steenrod algebra

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.1 (Sq0 is eventually isomorphic on the Ext groups.) Let Im(Sq0)i denote the image of (Sq0)i on ExtsA(F2, F2). Then, for arbitrary s, there exists a number r = r(s) depending on s such that (Sq0)i-r : Im(Sq0)r -> Im(Sq0)i is an isomorphism for every i >= r.
In other words, the conjecture predicts that any finite Sq0-family in ExtsA(F2, F2) has at most r(s) nonzero elements.

accepted.question_text: For the algebraic transfer tau_{s,t}: Hom_A^{t-s}(H_*((Z/2)^s; F_2), F_2)^{GL_s(Z/2)} -> Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2), prove or disprove the vanishing conjecture that Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2) = 0 whenever alpha(t) > s, where alpha(t) is the number of 1s in the binary expansion of t.
accepted.context_brief: vanishing line for Ext over the Steenrod algebra

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1 Prove or disprove the conjecture that Exts,tA(F2, F2) = 0 if α(t) > s, where, as usual, α(t) = k if t = 2i1 + ··· + 2ik with i1 < ... ik.
Note that Reg Wood's verification of the Peterson conjecture shows that the domain of τs,t is 0 if α(t) > s, and I am conjecturing that the range of τs,t vanishes in these same places.

accepted.question_text: Can the bigraded algebraic transfer tau^{*,*} be realized as the edge homomorphism of a spectral sequence in a way that gives a sensible measure of how far tau^{*,*} is from being an isomorphism of bigraded algebras?
accepted.context_brief: spectral sequence interpretation of the algebraic transfer

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2 Can τ*,* be viewed as the edge homomorphism of some spectral sequence?
This problem is not so well posed, but the point would be to find some sensible way to measure the failure of τ*,* to be an isomorphism of bigraded algebras.

accepted.question_text: Fix s. Is there a calculation of Ext_A^{s,*}(F_p, F_p) that is uniform for all sufficiently large primes p? In other words, for fixed Adams filtration s, does the structure of Ext_A^{s,*}(F_p, F_p) eventually become independent of p for large enough p, analogous to the stated behavior of Ext_A^{1,*}(F_p, F_p) for p > 2?
accepted.context_brief: large-prime uniformity of Ext over the Steenrod algebra

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3 Fix s. Is there a uniform calculation of Exts,*A(Fp, Fp) for all large enough p?
For example, Ext1,*A(Fp, Fp) can be viewed as 'independent of p' for p > 2.

accepted.question_text: For each s, is the algebraic transfer Tr_s: F_2 tensor_{GL_s} P H_*(B V_s) -> Ext_A^{s,s+*}(F_2, F_2) injective? Equivalently, does Singer's open conjecture hold that Tr_s is a monomorphism for every s?
accepted.context_brief: Singer conjecture on injectivity of the algebraic transfer

evidence.quote: Although Singer recognizes that Tr5 is not isomorphic, his open conjecture predicts that Trs is a monomorphism for any s.

accepted.question_text: Let p be a prime, let P_* be the polynomial part of the dual Steenrod algebra with P_* congruent to F_p[xi_1, xi_2, xi_3, ...], let P be its dual Hopf algebra, and consider Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p). The p-th power map on P_* induces an endomorphism P^0: Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p) -> Ext_P^{s,pt}(F_p, F_p). For fixed s > 0, is every element z in Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p) eventually sent to a nilpotent element by some iterate of P^0; equivalently, whenever z lies in the preimage (P^0)^-1 Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p), must z be nilpotent?
accepted.context_brief: nilpotence under the P^0 endomorphism on Ext over P

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.1 Fix s > 0. For all z ∈ (P0)-1Exts,tP(Fp, Fp), z is nilpotent. Equivalently, for all z ∈ Exts,tP(Fp, Fp), there exists an n ≥ 0 so that (P0)n z is nilpotent.

accepted.question_text: In the setting of Conjecture 4.1, can one always choose the iterate n to be 1? That is, for every z in Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p), is P^0 z already nilpotent after a single application of P^0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.3 In Conjecture 4.1, one may take n to be 1. That is, for all z ∈ Exts,tP(Fp, Fp), P0z is nilpotent.

accepted.question_text: Let p = 2 and G_{2n} = GL_{2n}(F_2). Let A_{n,n} be the maximal elementary 2-subgroup consisting of block upper triangular matrices with identity blocks on the diagonal, so that H^*(A_{n,n}; F_2) = F_2[x_{i,j} | 1 <= i,j <= n], and let det_n = det(x_{i,j}) be the degree-n class in the invariants H^n(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n}. If res: H^*(G_{2n}; F_2) -> H^*(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n} is the restriction homomorphism, is det_n in the image of res?
accepted.context_brief: restriction image for determinant classes in group cohomology

evidence.quote: We consider the image in dimension n. Let detn = det xi,j Then detn ∈ Hn(An,n; F2)Gn×Gn.

accepted.question_text: Let p = 2 and G_{2n} = GL_{2n}(F_2). Is the degree-n homology group H_n(G_{2n}; F_2) one-dimensional over F_2 and generated by the determinant class det_n arising from the maximal elementary 2-subgroup A_{n,n}?
accepted.context_brief: generation of H_n(GL_{2n}(F_2); F_2) by det_n

evidence.quote: Question 5.2 Is Hn(G2n; F2) = F2 generated by detn ?

accepted.question_text: Let E be the extraspecial p-group p^(1+2)_+ of order p^3 and exponent p for an odd prime p. A graph in Theorem 6.2 of the cited companion paper describes the stable splitting of B G for all p-local finite groups G having Sylow p-subgroup E when p = 3. Determine the analogous stable-splitting graph for p = 7, using Theorem 9.4 from the same paper as a partial input.
accepted.context_brief: stable splitting graph for p-local finite groups over an extraspecial p-group

evidence.quote: The problem is to write down the similar graph for p = 7. A partial result is given in Theorem 9.4 in the same paper.

Let us write by E the extraspecial p-group p1+2+ of order p3 and exponent p for an odd prime p. In Theorem 6.2 of my paper in the present proceedings ... we have a graph which shows stable splitting of BG for all (p-local) finite groups having a Sylow p-subgroup E for p = 3.
